title: Check yourself: When a batch fits, how to meet an SLA with it, and what to resubmit

questions.stem: Scenario S5, Claude Code in CI. A pipeline runs two Claude jobs: a verdict that a pull request needs before it may merge, and a Sunday scan of every service for outdated patterns. A manager wants both moved to the discounted bulk queue. What should the architect do?

options.text: Keep the first on the immediate API and send the second through a batch
options.says: A merge verdict is a blocking check that cannot wait for a window without a latency guarantee, while the weekly scan can wait.

options.text: Move both, since half the price outweighs a wait of unknown length
options.says: Ruled out because "It is not a reason to move work that cannot" wait, whatever the discount.

options.text: Put the first through a batch and keep the second on the immediate API
options.says: Ruled out because "a blocking check cannot wait for a window that has no latency guarantee", and this option sends exactly that check there.

options.text: Move both, but submit a batch every hour so that the wait stays short
options.says: Ruled out because "the window is a ceiling and not a promise of an hour", so more frequent submissions do not give the verdict a deadline.

questions.stem: Scenario S6, structured data extraction. A contract-intake service promises that every uploaded document is extracted within 30 hours. Extraction runs as batches that finish within 24 hours, and the results take 2 hours to validate and deliver. What is the longest gap, in hours, between batch submissions that still keeps the promise?

options.says: Ruled out because "worst-case wait = submission interval + processing window + handling time" includes the 24-hour window, which 28 ignores.
Ruled out because "a nightly batch gives a worst wait of 24 + 24 + handling, which is 50 hours".
The worst case is the interval plus the window plus the handling, so 30 minus 24 minus 2 leaves 4.
Ruled out because the arithmetic starts from "2 hours to read and deliver the results", which 6 leaves out.
